newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The UAE ministry of health said on Monday there were no immediate plans to ban smoking in public or enclosed places.
- Services in Bahrain's ports are to be leased to the private sector as part of wide-ranging moves to boost the island's trade and economy, officials said.
- Software piracy in the Arab World is expected to decline by five percent in 1997, the Business Software Alliance said.
- Sharjah Airport saw a 28.3 percent increase in air cargo tonnage handled during the first half of 1997 compared with the same period a year earlier, the airport said.
- The UAE has drafted an anti-money laundering law as part of reforms in the financial sector.
- The last few days have witnessed a steady increase in the subscription for shares in the Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank, which is reported to be heavily oversubscribed.
- Sharjah's banking sector has grown by 6.9 percent in 1995 compared with 1994, the Sharjah Economic Department said.
- Subscription in Abu Dhabi's Saadiyat Free Zone opens in September.
- Internet fees in the UAE down by 12.5 percent.
